findings.title: Local .env secrets are not excluded from Git
findings.what: .env.example instructs operators to create a repository-root .env, but the ignore rules cover dependencies, build outputs, and *.local without excluding .env. Auth tokens, API keys, TLS settings, and passwords placed there can therefore be staged and committed accidentally.
findings.fix: Add a root-scoped `/.env` ignore rule, while retaining `.env.example` as the committed template.
findings.acceptance: After creating an untracked root `.env`, `git check-ignore -v .env` identifies the new rule, while `git check-ignore .env.example` reports no match.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read .gitignore:10-18 and .env.example:1-2 at baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba; no existing .env exclusion survives in the dispatched ignore file.

findings.title: Build context includes the credential-bearing .env file
findings.what: The local/staged-data and secret exclusions do not include `.env`. Both Dockerfiles later use `COPY . .`, so an operator's Compose credential file is sent to the container builder and retained in the build stage even though the final stage copies selected outputs.
findings.fix: Add `/.env` and appropriate private-key/certificate patterns to .dockerignore before any broad `COPY . .`.
findings.acceptance: With a sentinel root `.env`, a build-context listing or guarded test proves `.env` is excluded, and neither Dockerfile can read the sentinel after `COPY . .`.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read .dockerignore:14-20 and confirmed the dispatched file excludes only public, *.local, and Tailscale-specific TLS names in this section; the root .env remains unmatched.

findings.title: Container base images are not digest-pinned
findings.what: The server image uses `node:24-slim` for both stages, while the SPA uses `node:24-slim` and `docker.io/nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27-alpine`. These mutable tags can resolve to different bytes across otherwise identical builds, weakening reproducibility and allowing upstream tag movement to alter the trusted runtime.
findings.fix: Pin every FROM reference to an approved immutable sha256 digest and update digests through a reviewed dependency-update process.
findings.acceptance: A policy check parses both Dockerfiles and verifies every non-scratch FROM has an `@sha256:<64-hex>` digest; two clean builds resolve identical base manifests.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read all four FROM lines at the immutable baseline; none contains an OCI digest, and the SPA registry qualification does not make its tag immutable.

findings.title: SPA container ships without a liveness probe
findings.what: The standalone SPA image exposes port 8325 and relies on nginx's inherited command but defines no HEALTHCHECK. Orchestrators using image health metadata cannot distinguish a serving nginx instance from a wedged or misconfigured one.
findings.fix: Add a lightweight localhost health check against a static asset or dedicated endpoint, with explicit interval, timeout, start period, and retries.
findings.acceptance: Inspecting the built SPA image shows a non-empty healthcheck, and stopping or breaking nginx causes the container health state to transition to unhealthy within the configured budget.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read Dockerfile.spa:60-69 through EOF; the shipped runtime has COPY and EXPOSE instructions but no HEALTHCHECK, unlike Dockerfile:97-105.
